data.narrative:
Nth Cycle is a Growth-stage climate and energy company founded by Megan O'Connor and Chad Vecitis, having raised $60M in equity alongside a 10-year offtake agreement with Trafigura valued at $1.1B. The Climate & Energy sector includes 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linamar, LNZA), though peers range widely in maturity and business model.

A peer-median valuation method is not applicable here. The company operates at a stage and scale without sufficient comparable datapoints—zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier peers were identified within the narrowly-defined Climate & Energy cohort. While broader private peers exist (Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Enovix), their heterogeneity in stage, technology, and capital structures prevents reliable triangulation. An all-sector median would introduce material noise and mask the idiosyncratic risk profile of Nth Cycle's business model.

Without sufficient peer clustering, standard DCF or revenue multiple approaches would require ground-truth assumptions on unit economics, capex intensity, and offtake margin realization. The Trafigura agreement ($1.1B notional over 10 years) provides a revenue ceiling and demand signal, but its present value depends critically on assumptions about COGS, discount rates, and contract flexibility. Any valuation range would rest primarily on management's execution risk and commodity price exposure rather than market comparables. Further due diligence on offtake contract terms and competitive positioning is required to establish defensible value bounds.
